open_points.subject: customer erasure scope
open_points.text: “erase a customer's contact data” says “The Customer keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased” but enumerates only “name, phone, e-mail and language” as gone, after fiscal data and kind were added to the Customer
open_points.question: Does erasure also remove the customer's kind, tax id, legal name, restriction state and relationship-ended state, or do any of them survive?
options: Remove every field except customer_ref and the erased fact
Remove contact fields only and retain kind and fiscal/state fields
Remove all personal fields but retain non-personal lifecycle state
open_points.default_guess: Remove every field except customer_ref and the erased fact.

open_points.subject: billing-data read timing
open_points.text: The billing read is available to PresuPro “when it issues a document”, while R0-80 says “a draft, a preview or an unsent version ... reads it when rendered”
open_points.question: May PresuPro read billing data while rendering drafts and previews, or only at the act of issuance, and can Registry enforce that condition?
options: Allow reads for rendering and issuance as a token-level contractual purpose
Allow only an issuance operation that proves or performs issuance
Allow the token to read at any time and leave purpose limitation entirely to PresuPro
open_points.default_guess: Allow reads for rendering and issuance, with PresuPro contractually responsible for purpose limitation.

open_points.subject: agent personal-data boundary
open_points.text: The Agent actor says it “never receives a value Registry holds as personal_data”, but R0-74 says “What other services cleared for personal_data pass on to Kernel is bounded by their own contracts, not here”
open_points.question: Is preventing Cabinet, PresuPro or Client Portal from forwarding Registry personal data to Kernel or the agent part of the platform guarantee, and which named contract enforces it?
options: The guarantee is end-to-end and every trusted-service contract must prohibit forwarding
Registry guarantees only its direct responses; forwarding is outside this product's guarantee
Only Cabinet must prohibit forwarding because it directly integrates with Kernel
open_points.default_guess: Registry guarantees only direct responses, while Cabinet's separate contract must prohibit forwarding to Kernel or the agent.

open_points.subject: audit coverage
open_points.text: Registry records “significant changes of state: changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations”
open_points.question: Which exact primary actions create audit entries, especially room creation, artifact publication or withdrawal, session registration, active-project changes, access requests and answers, relationship changes, imports and archive replays?
options: Audit every accepted state-changing primary action
Audit only the categories explicitly enumerated, with an exact action mapping
Audit owner actions but not service or agent-authority actions except grants and revocations
open_points.default_guess: Define an exact mapping and audit every material accepted state change, excluding explicitly ordinary reads and no-op replays.

open_points.subject: audit atomicity
open_points.text: The text promises “a log entry for every erasure” and a log of significant changes, but does not say whether recording the entry is atomic with the state change
open_points.question: If an audit entry cannot be recorded, must the corresponding state change be refused and rolled back, or may it succeed without its required entry?
options: Audit entry and state mutation are one atomic transaction
Mutation succeeds and audit recording is retried
Only erasures require atomic audit; other entries are best effort
open_points.default_guess: Audit entry and audited state mutation are one atomic transaction.

open_points.subject: session access version
open_points.text: “read the session's access” returns “the access version”, but no text defines what changes that version
open_points.question: Which actions increment the access version, and do no-op or refused operations leave it unchanged?
options: Increment for granted-set or active-project changes only
Increment for every session-access mutation, including pending-request replacement or clearing
Use separate authorization and request versions
open_points.default_guess: Increment for every accepted mutation to the granted set, active project or pending request; no-ops and refusals do not increment it.

open_points.subject: duplicate grant semantics
open_points.text: “grant a project to an agent session” says “the project joins the session's granted set” but gives no outcome when it is already in that set
open_points.question: What happens when the owner grants an already-granted project, with or without asking to make it active?
options: Return the unchanged grant, while still applying an active-project change if requested
Refuse the duplicate grant
Treat the whole request as an idempotent replay only when every input matches
open_points.default_guess: Return the unchanged set and apply the requested active-project change if needed.

open_points.subject: answering an access request with an invalid project
open_points.text: “answer an access request” says granting adds “the project the owner picks from the catalogue”, while its only stated failure is “a request no longer pending refused”
open_points.question: What happens if the selected project is unknown, archived, anonymised, already granted, or becomes unavailable between display and confirmation?
options: Apply the same validation and duplicate semantics as direct grant
Allow any catalogue selection captured when the form was rendered
Clear the request even when the grant cannot be applied
open_points.default_guess: Apply direct-grant validation atomically and leave the pending request unchanged on failure.

open_points.subject: active-project and revocation edge cases
open_points.text: “change the active project or revoke a project” states failures only for “a project not in the set” and an archived project being made active
open_points.question: What are the outcomes for an unknown session, an unknown project, setting the already-active project, clearing an already-empty active project, and revoking a granted project that is not active?
options: Define idempotent no-ops for same-active and already-clear, refuse unknown session/project, and allow revoking any granted project
Refuse every request that makes no state change
Use one generic not-granted response for all unknown-session and unknown-project cases
open_points.default_guess: Refuse unknown sessions and projects, allow revoking any granted project, and treat same-active or already-clear changes as unchanged successes.

open_points.subject: restriction transition semantics
open_points.text: “restrict or lift a restriction on a customer” does not say what happens when restricting an already-restricted customer or lifting a restriction that is not present
open_points.question: Are repeated restriction and lift requests idempotent successes, or are invalid state transitions refused, and do successful no-ops move the customer revision?
options: Both repeats return unchanged and do not move the revision
Both invalid transitions are refused
Repeats succeed and move the revision
open_points.default_guess: Return unchanged without moving the revision.

open_points.subject: relationship transition and date input
open_points.text: “end or resume a customer relationship” outputs “marked as ended on that date, or the mark cleared” without naming the source of the date or repeated-transition behavior
open_points.question: Is the end date supplied by the owner or assigned by Registry, and what happens when ending an already-ended relationship or resuming one that is not ended?
options: Owner supplies the effective date; repeated transitions are unchanged successes
Registry records the current date; repeated transitions are unchanged successes
Registry records the current timestamp; repeated transitions are refused
open_points.default_guess: The owner supplies the effective date, and repeated transitions return unchanged without moving the revision.

open_points.subject: anonymised project artifact pointers
open_points.text: R0-71 says an anonymised project “holds no personal value”, while R0-62 retains artifact pointers and R0-68 says a pointer value that breaks the writer rule “is not refused and does reach the agent”
open_points.question: What must happen when retained pointer fields contain identifying or personal text: refuse anonymisation, remove or redact pointers, require an owner attestation, or accept that the result may not be anonymous?
options: Refuse anonymisation unless the owner confirms the retained pointers are non-identifying
Remove or redact identifying pointer values during anonymisation
Keep pointers without inspection and treat anonymity as solely a governance assertion
Require whole deletion whenever pointer safety cannot be established
open_points.default_guess: Require owner confirmation that retained pointers are non-identifying, otherwise use whole deletion.

open_points.subject: service copy-removal target
open_points.text: The product target says “no other service keeps a customer record or a copy of these values” and R0-81 says “Each service removes its own customer records and copies in its own case”
open_points.question: What observable fact establishes that each service has reached the target, who records it, and what happens if a service continues retaining copies beyond its listed transition?
options: Governance records a per-service completion assertion and blocks no Registry operation
A verified service release and migration result close each listed copy
Registry withholds personal-data access until the service proves copy removal
open_points.default_guess: A verified service release and migration result close each governance-listed copy; Registry continues operating during the transition.
